title: Weekly camera detections of 9 mammal and lizard taxa at 5 road underpasses and 6 forest sites, Port Macquarie, NSW, 165 weeks
creator: Goldingay, Ross L.; Rohweder, David; Taylor, Brendan D.; Parkyn, Jonathan L.
citation: Goldingay, R. L., Rohweder, D., Taylor, B. D., & Parkyn, J. L. (2022). Use of road underpasses by mammals and a monitor lizard in eastern Australia and consideration of the prey-trap hypothesis [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.cvdncjt6m
abstract: Weekly detection/non-detection of macropods, bandicoots, possums, predators and the lace monitor from camera traps in road underpasses and at random forest sites along the Oxley Highway at Port Macquarie (5 underpasses, 6 forest sites; 31.46 S, 152.84 E), New South Wales, Australia, 2013-2017.
samplingProtocol: Reconyx (and one KeepGuard) cameras inside underpasses and at random forest clearings within 100 m of the road; passes of each species collated per site (30-minute independence) and converted to weekly detection histories; weeks without a working camera marked missing.
closureNote: weekly detections over three to four years; the authors compared the proportion of weeks used, not a closed-season occupancy
geographicCoverage: Oxley Highway at Port Macquarie (5 underpasses, 6 forest sites; 31.46 S, 152.84 E)

notShipped.season_row: the lace monitor files' spring/summer flag row (derivable from date)
notShipped.inconsistent_weeks: site-weeks marked missing for some species but not others: dropped for all (shared-detector ruling)

notes: Forest cameras ran in different weeks from the underpass cameras (at Grafton they overlapped for 11 weeks), so most weeks have only one site type. taxonInclusion = target: the species analysed by the authors, not every species photographed.
